domain: Pre-built faceted search landing pages at scale
summary: The prior auditor's core structural findings survive verification: one faceted engine at app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx (1077 lines, confirmed), zero generateStaticParams on that route (confirmed), a 35-preset flat registry (confirmed, exactly 35 entries), and city x preset plus city x subdivision in the XML sitemap but never the 3-way combination. Three things they got wrong or missed. (1) They called the internal-linking picture emptier than it is — grepping only for the symbols getAllPresetSlugs/SEARCH_PRESETS made them miss lib/site-menu.ts, which hardcodes 13 Bend preset facet URLs into the site-wide mega-menu rendered by components/site/SiteHeader.tsx:94, and lib/popular-searches.ts, a 10-city x 10-preset curated registry that feeds the search page's Related searches block. (2) They mischaracterized the caching: this route awaits searchParams on every render, so under Next 16 `export const revalidate = 60` does not produce ISR-cached full-route entries — the actual caching is the CDN header `s-maxage=60` in next.config for /homes-for-sale/:path*, which also means personalized signed-in renders share a public cache key. (3) They missed that the ONLY sold/closed facet entry point in the whole site is broken: the footer's "Sold homes" link, the mega-menu's "Recently sold", and the /sold redirect all point to /homes-for-sale?status=Sold, and `status` is never read anywhere in the route (only `statusFilter` is), so all three silently render active inventory. They also missed a mechanical gate — scripts/static-params-baseline.json grandfathers app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx as an accepted static-params violator, making "no pre-building" a knowingly-accepted debt rather than an oversight.

items.requirement: Faceted/intent search routes exist as real, crawlable URLs (not query-param only)
items.evidence: app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx confirmed 1077 lines. resolveSlugImpl at lines 102-145 parses 1-3 segments into city / neighborhood-or-subdivision / preset exactly as claimed (neighborhood wins over same-named preset at lines 125-129). next.config rewrites confirmed at lines 216-217 (`/homes-for-sale` -> `/search`, `/homes-for-sale/:path*` -> `/search/:path*`) and redirects at lines 149-150 push /search/* back to /homes-for-sale/*. robots.ts allows `/` for all crawlers with no /homes-for-sale disallow. Preset property-type coverage confirmed: lib/search-presets.ts:103 lots-and-land (propertyType Land), :107 condos, :108 townhomes — 3 of 35. lib/property-type-labels.ts:15,24,42 map MFR/MF/B to Multi-Family and :25-27,46 map MFD/MH/MHP to Manufactured, so the vocabulary exists unused.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor called the missing status facet a mere absence. It is worse — it is advertised and broken.] Everything they said about thin property-type coverage holds. But the sold/closed facet is not simply absent: lib/site-nav.ts:153 ships a footer link `/homes-for-sale?status=Sold` labelled "Sold homes", lib/site-menu.ts:218 ships a mega-menu link `/homes-for-sale?status=Sold` labelled "Recently sold", and next.config:148 redirects `/sold` to the same URL. The route never reads a `status` param — grep of app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx returns only `sp.statusFilter` (lines 329, 357, 652, 944), and lib/search/field-registry.ts has no `status` key. All three entry points render plain active inventory under a "Sold homes" label. Additionally, `status` is absent from the 24 blockedKeys in lib/seo-routing.ts:13-41, so that URL is fully indexable while being a duplicate of /homes-for-sale.

items.requirement: Pages are statically generated (pre-built) and in the sitemap, not client-side/query-param-only
items.evidence: Confirmed: `grep -rln generateStaticParams app/` returns 16 files and app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx is NOT among them. The route has only `export const revalidate = 60` (line 269) and no `dynamic`/`dynamicParams` export. New evidence the auditor missed: scripts/check-static-params.mjs is wired into `ci:gates` (package.json:171, via `ci:static-params` at :68) and scripts/static-params-baseline.json (generatedAt 2026-07-19) explicitly lists "app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx" among 19 grandfathered violators. next.config:131 sets `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=600` on /homes-for-sale/:path*.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor's mechanism is wrong — this is not ISR.] The conclusion (nothing is pre-built) is right, the explanation is not. Both `generateMetadata` and the page component await `searchParams` (page.tsx lines 158-160, 273-274), which under Next 16 (package.json:330) forces dynamic rendering — `revalidate = 60` cannot populate a full-route cache entry for these URLs. What actually absorbs crawler load is the CDN header at next.config:131, not ISR. Two consequences they never surfaced: (a) that `public, s-maxage=60` header applies to every /homes-for-sale/* response including signed-in renders that call getSession, getSavedListingKeys, getLikedListingKeys and getBuyingPreferences (page.tsx imports at lines 18, 63-65), so personalized markup is shared-cacheable; (b) the missing pre-build is a knowingly-accepted debt tracked in scripts/static-params-baseline.json, not an oversight — the gate will block a NEW violator but permanently permits this one.

items.requirement: Thousands of pre-built URLs: every city, every community, every subdivision, crossed with property type and status facets
items.evidence: app/sitemap.ts verified line by line. Static tier: SITE_CITY_SLUGS loop at 226-232 emits /cities, /homes-for-sale, /open-houses per city and NO preset URLs. Dynamic tier: cities derived from a live active-listings scan at 264-278, then city x preset at 288-297 via getAllPresetSlugs(). RESORT_COMMUNITY_SLUGS is a 14-entry const at 23-28 emitted at 303-310. City x subdivision at 312-339 from one (City, SubdivisionName) scan. Listings from listing_tile_mv at 362-405. lib/search-presets.ts has exactly 35 preset entries (verified by count) and getAllPresetSlugs at :142-144.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor missed a single-point-of-failure that can zero out the entire faceted sitemap.] Their arithmetic and the missing 3-way combination are confirmed. What they missed: the whole dynamic block sits inside ONE try/catch (app/sitemap.ts:244 ... 473-476) whose first await is `getCommunitiesForSitemapJoin(5000)` at line 248. Any throw there — before the city loop at 280 ever runs — drops EVERY city x preset URL, every subdivision URL, every listing URL, and every blog/guide/report URL in one silent `console.error`, leaving only the ~10-city static tier. The city x preset block is fed exclusively by the dynamic `cities` array from the listings scan (line 289 is inside the 280 loop); the resilient SITE_CITY_SLUGS loop at 226-232 emits zero preset URLs, so the resilience the comment at 223-225 claims for city hubs does not extend to any facet page. The file comment at 33-38 asserting "total URLs are well under Google's 50,000 limit" is an unverified assumption with no count guard.

items.requirement: A taxonomy/registry defining facet combinations (property type x status x geo)
items.evidence: lib/search-presets.ts confirmed: 35 flat entries, SearchPreset.params carries optional propertyType (:51) and propertySubType (:44) alongside price/amenity/sort keys, PRESET_BY_SLUG map at :129, getPresetBySlug/isPresetSlug/getAllPresetSlugs at :131-144. Test file lib/search-presets.test.ts asserts unique slugs and length >= 15 only. A second, richer registry the auditor did not mention: lib/popular-searches.ts CITY_POPULAR_SEARCHES, 10 cities (bend, redmond, sisters, sunriver, la-pine, prineville, madras, terrebonne, powell-butte, culver) x 10 ordered preset slugs each, with a documented live-inventory provenance trace in the header comment (lines 9-26).
items.gap: [CORRECTED: there IS a second, city-scoped facet registry the auditor never found.] Their structural conclusion stands — SEARCH_PRESETS is a flat overloaded preset list, not an orthogonal propertyType x status x geo product, and nothing composes two facets. But lib/popular-searches.ts is a real curated geo x facet mapping (100 city-preset pairs, inventory-grounded) that they missed entirely, and it is the correct seed for both a generateStaticParams enumeration and any future taxonomy. What is genuinely absent: no status dimension of any kind (the 'pending' preset is the only status-ish slug and there is no sold/closed/coming-soon preset), no multi-family or manufactured preset, and no subdivision-level entry in popular-searches.ts, so the 3-way combination has no registry to draw from.

items.requirement: A site index so users and crawlers can reach faceted pages not in the nav
items.evidence: [Auditor's grep was too narrow.] lib/site-menu.ts:122-124 defines bendPreset() and lines 141-195 hardcode 13 Bend facet URLs into MENU (new-listings, under-500k, under-750k, under-1m, luxury, over-2m, on-golf-course, mountain-view, river-view, single-level, acreage, new-construction, condos). MENU is imported by components/site/SiteHeader.tsx:6 and rendered at :94 (MegaMenu) and :118 (MobileNav) — a site-wide, every-page facet link block. app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx:693 calls getPopularSearchesForCity(relatedCitySlug, 12) for the Related searches rail, so any city page cross-links up to 8 of its own facet pages. app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx:623-627 confirmed: exactly 5 hardcoded preset anchors. Confirmed absent: no /browse, no /sitemap HTML page, nothing in app/ resembling a directory; lib/site-nav.ts FOOTER_NAV (:145-210) carries zero preset links.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: status raised from missing to partial — 13 facet URLs are in the site-wide nav on every page, which the auditor asserted did not exist.] Still not a site index. The mega-menu coverage is Bend-only (bendPreset() hardcodes `/homes-for-sale/bend`, site-menu.ts:119), so 9 of the 10 cities in lib/popular-searches.ts have zero nav-level facet links. Worse, lib/data/nav/getMegaMenuData.ts:254 builds per-city popularSearches for every HOMES_CITY_SLUGS entry and is exported from lib/data/index.ts:239 — but grep across app/ and components/ finds NO consumer: SiteHeader passes the static MENU instead. That is dead code that would have solved the per-city nav gap. And the 3-way path (/homes-for-sale/bend/tetherow/townhomes) remains reachable only by hand-typed URL: not in the sitemap, not in MENU, not in popular-searches, not in the city hub.

items.requirement: Geo pages link to their faceted children; faceted pages link to related blog content
items.evidence: City hub preset links confirmed at app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx:623-627 (5 anchors) plus the all-homes CTA at :612. Search-route cross-links confirmed: relatedSearches at page.tsx:691-694, presetBandLinks/presetCityLinks at :757-760 via lib/site/preset-faq.ts getAdjacentPriceBandLinks/getSamePresetCityLinks. Blog absence confirmed by grep: app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx contains no blog_posts, no guides, no KbArticles import — the only Kb import is KbFooter (line 23, rendered at 430 and 1073).
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Every claim checks out. Adding one they missed: the same-preset city cross-link helper (getSamePresetCityLinks) means preset pages DO fan out horizontally across cities, which is the strongest internal-link signal on the route — but it fires only when isPresetDepthPage is true (page.tsx:743-753), which requires no subdivision segment and a clean query string, so a subdivision-level facet page gets zero cross-links of any kind. Facet-page-to-blog linking is entirely absent as stated.

items.requirement: Index-bloat controls: canonical tags, noindex for empty results, pagination handling
items.evidence: lib/seo-routing.ts:8-46 confirmed: page>1 plus 24 blocked query keys. app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx generateMetadata:155-214 read in full — it applies robots {index:false, follow:true} when shouldNoIndexSearchVariant(sp) or hasInvalidPresetSegment, sets a self-referential canonical via buildCanonicalPath (:147-153), and confirmed contains NO listings fetch and NO count of any kind. isPresetDepthPage (:743-753) gates on city && !subdivision && preset && !isSortOnlyPreset && !shouldNoIndexSearchVariant — no count term. lib/site/preset-faq.ts:266-294 confirmed: `count === 0` produces "No {plural} are on the market in {city} right now" plus a full FAQ, still emitted through FAQBlock as FAQPage JSON-LD on an indexable page.
items.gap: [VERIFIED, and the auditor understated it.] Everything they wrote is accurate. Two additions. First, `status` is missing from the blockedKeys list in lib/seo-routing.ts:13-41, so the site's own footer and mega-menu links to /homes-for-sale?status=Sold are indexable duplicates of /homes-for-sale (the canonical does point back correctly, which limits the damage). Second, the page body DOES have totalCount in hand and passes it to buildPresetFaq (page.tsx:756) — so the data needed for a count-aware noindex is already resolved server-side. The blocker is purely that generateMetadata runs as a separate function with its own resolveSlug and never touches the listings fetch. This is a genuinely small fix (hoist the count into the request-scoped cache() the way resolveSlug already is at page.tsx:96-99), which supports their S estimate.

shared_primitives_needed: A geo x facet taxonomy registry with independent propertyType and status enums, seeded from the existing lib/popular-searches.ts city-preset pairs rather than built from scratch, so blog internal-linking, CMA comps, and market reports share one facet vocabulary.

A result-count-aware indexability helper that wraps shouldNoIndexSearchVariant and takes a count, callable from generateMetadata — requires hoisting the listings count into a request-scoped cache() shared between generateMetadata and the page body (the resolveSlug pattern at app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx:96-99 is the working template).

A generateStaticParams enumeration source for the top facet combinations; lib/popular-searches.ts already encodes 100 inventory-grounded city x preset pairs and is the obvious input. Landing it requires removing app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx from scripts/static-params-baseline.json.
A canonical status facet (active / pending / sold / coming-soon) as a real path segment, because three shipped nav surfaces already promise sold inventory and silently deliver active listings.
A sitemap resilience pattern: per-section try/catch instead of the single wrapping try in app/sitemap.ts:244, so one failing query cannot silently drop every faceted URL from the sitemap.
open_questions_for_owner: The footer, the mega-menu, and the /sold redirect all advertise sold homes and all render active inventory. Do you want a real sold/closed facet as a path segment (indexable, sitemapped), or should those three links be pulled until one exists?

Should the 3-way city x subdivision x preset combination be enumerated for every subdivision with live inventory, or only for the curated 14 resort communities? This is the difference between hundreds and thousands of URLs.

Is it acceptable to index a facet page with zero current inventory, or should those noindex until they carry at least N live listings? The FAQ copy already handles the zero case honestly, so this is purely an indexation call.

Do you want net-new property-type facets (multi-family, manufactured) bolted onto the existing 35-preset list, or a structurally separate property-type dimension that composes with the amenity and price presets? The latter is a rewrite of the slug resolver.

lib/data/nav/getMegaMenuData.ts already builds per-city popular searches for every city and is wired to nothing — the header renders the Bend-only static MENU instead. Was that deliberate (menu simplicity) or an unfinished migration? Wiring it would give all 10 cities nav-level facet links for near-zero cost.
